_DOCTRINE: Every article REPORTS MECHANICS and never makes the call. The call is the book's. check-noconnect.py must exit 0 before any of these enters an import batch. A fact with value null DELETES its sentence — it is never softened to 'sometimes' or 'often'. No drift-prone value in a title, heading or excerpt: they cannot carry a fact-span.
_WHY_THESE_FIVE: S-insure is the widest gap in the corpus (932 dedicated words) and the highest stakes. The existing turkey-health-guide prescribes bottled water and nothing else; what a US traveler is actually exposed to, what a policy pays, and what voids it appear nowhere. These five report the components separately. The book connects them.

articles.title: What to Expect When a Turkish Hospital Bills You
reports: the three hospital types (Devlet / Ozel / university) and who bills whom
the emergency obligation: admission and intervention are unconditional, charges are collected AFTER care
that emergency transport itself is chargeable, unlike the emergency care obligation
deposit / prepayment / guarantee-of-payment practice for NON-emergency treatment
direct billing vs pay-and-claim, and which groups do which
that pricing under tourist health sits in a Ministry of Health framework rather than a published hospital tariff — which is why no figure can be quoted in advance
articles.must_not_say: any price figure, any version of 'so buy travel insurance', and no conflation of medical-tourism rules with tourist health
articles._REVISED: Was 'What Healthcare Actually Costs in Turkey Without Insurance'. All four price facts came back null from BOTH panel models — no public self-pay tariff exists. Prices deleted, not estimated. The article now reports the billing MECHANICS, and the absence of a quotable price becomes the finding.

articles.title: What a Standard US Travel Policy Pays For in Turkey
reports: the four coverage heads a traveler meets: medical, evacuation, trip cancellation, baggage
primary vs secondary coverage and what that means when a US health plan is involved
direct billing vs pay-and-claim — which Turkish hospitals do which
the documents a claim needs, gathered at the time, not after
articles.must_not_say: which policy or provider to buy; no policy is arbitrated

articles.title: The Activities That Void Travel Insurance in Turkey
reports: the standard exclusion families: motorised two-wheelers, unlicensed operation, altitude/aviation, watersports, alcohol
how the balloon flight is classified across policy wordings (aviation vs adventure activity vs excluded)
the scooter/quad case: the licence condition inside the exclusion, not the exclusion itself
paragliding at Ölüdeniz, diving, and where operator insurance ends and yours begins
articles.must_not_say: 'check your policy' as a conclusion, or any margin/sequencing rule
articles.note: This is the article that makes the balloon a node in S-insure. It reports how the balloon is CLASSIFIED. It does not say what to do about it.

articles.title: Getting Treated in Turkey: Pharmacies, Clinics and the ER
reports: the eczane system: what a pharmacist can dispense and decide without a doctor
nöbetçi eczane (duty pharmacy) — how the rota works out of hours
walk-in private clinic vs hospital ER: cost, wait, English availability
prescription rules for medication a traveler already carries
articles.must_not_say: a recommended first stop — reporting the ladder is not ranking it

articles.title: Bringing Medication into Turkey
reports: controlled/restricted categories and the documentation each needs
quantity limits and original-packaging rules
what a doctor's letter must contain to be useful at the border
which common US prescriptions are restricted or unavailable in Turkey
articles.must_not_say: reassurance ('you'll be fine') or a blanket warning — report the rule or delete the sentence
